chunks: (13) And Ali ibn Ahmad informed us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa informed us, from a man, from al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from ar-Rabee' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Muhzim ibn Abu Burda al-Asadi and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

By Allah, you will be broken like glass, and indeed glass is remade and returns as it was. By Allah, you will be broken like pottery, for indeed pottery breaks and does not return as it was. By Allah, you will be sifted, and by Allah you will be distinguished, and by Allah you will be purified until none of you remain except the fewest. And he shook his hand.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the glass and pottery metaphor in the hadith about the Shia during the occultation?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) employs the metaphors of glass and pottery to illustrate the varying degrees of fidelity among the Shia during the Minor Occultation. The 'glass' represents those who waver but ultimately return to the truth, while the 'pottery' signifies those who apostatize and remain in disbelief, never to be restored. This narrative underscores the historical reality of the 'Ghabr al-Shi'a' (the sifted Shia), emphasizing that the occultation serves as a divine trial to purify the community, leaving only the steadfast remnant.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (13) Ali bin Ahmad narrated from Obaydillah bin Musa from someone from al-Abbas bin Aamir from ar-Rabee’ bin Muhammad al-Musli from Muhzim bin Abu Burda al-Asadi and others that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said:

“By Allah, you are going to be broken like glass but glass is remade and it returns as before. By Allah, you are going to be broken like the breaking of pottery but pottery is never remade as before. By Allah you are going to be sifted, to be clarified and to be purified until none of you remain save the least. (He shrank his hand.)” O people of Shia, pay much attention to these traditions narrated from Amirul Mo’mineen (as) and the infallible imams (as) after him. Ponder on them too much. They warn strongly of turning away from their Sharia by saying: “one believes in our matter in the morning and recants it in the evening or he believes in it in the evening and when morning comes he recants it.” It is a clear evidence showing neglecting the system of the imamate with all its concerns that lead to the straight path. Then Amirul Mo’mineen (as) gives an example when saying: “By Allah, you are going to be broken like glass but glass is remade and it returns as before. By Allah, you are going to be broken like the breaking of pottery but pottery is never remade as before.” Those, who believe in the doctrine of the infallible imams and then recant it and then they repent and return to the true belief when the mercy of Allah declares to them the purity of what they deny and the darkness of what they enter into, are like broken glass that it can be remade as before but those, who recant the true belief and remain in their confusion without repenting until death, are like broken pottery that cannot be remade as before because there is no repent after death.
